title.zh: 卷359 列傳一百四十六 岳起 荆道乾 谢启昆 李殿图 张师诚 王绍兰 李奕畴 钱楷 和舜武
title.en: Volume 359 Biographies 146: Yue Qi, Jing Daoqian, Xie Qikun, Li Diantu, Zhang Shicheng, Wang Shaolan, Li Yichou, Qian Kai, He Shunwu
title.raw: 卷359 列傳一百四十六 岳起 荆道乾 谢启昆 李殿图 张师诚 王绍兰 李奕畴 钱楷 和舜武

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十六

translations.literal: Biographies 146
translations.idiomatic: Biography 146

sentences.zh: 岳起荊道乾謝啟昆李殿圖張師誠王紹蘭

translations.literal: Yue Qi, Jing Daoqian, Xie Qikun, Li Diantu, Zhang Shicheng, Wang Shaolan
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi, Jing Daoqian, Xie Qikun, Li Diantu, Zhang Shicheng, and Wang Shaolan

sentences.zh: 李奕疇錢楷和舜武

translations.literal: Li Yichou, Qian Kai, He Shunwu
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichou, Qian Kai, and He Shunwu

sentences.zh: 岳起，鄂濟氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Yue Qi, of the Eji clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi, of the Eji clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年舉人，議敘，授筆帖式。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate; by examination for service he was appointed a Secretariat copyist.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign he passed the provincial examinations; through seniority review he received appointment as a Secretariat copyist.

sentences.zh: 累擢戶部員外郎、翰林院侍講學士、詹事府少詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting, and Junior Vice-Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy, and junior vice-director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，遷奉天府尹。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he was transferred to be Fengtian prefectural governor (Fengtian yin).
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he was appointed prefectural governor (Fengtian yin) of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 前官貪黷，岳起至，屋宇器用遍洗滌之，曰：「勿染其污跡也！」

translations.literal: His predecessor had been corrupt; when Yue Qi arrived he had every building and utensil thoroughly washed, saying: 'Do not let their tainted traces stain you!'
translations.idiomatic: The previous incumbent had been corrupt; when Yue Qi took office he had every room and piece of equipment scrubbed clean, saying, "Do not let their filth touch you!"

sentences.zh: 與將軍忤。

translations.literal: He came into conflict with the general.
translations.idiomatic: He fell out with the garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 逾年，擢內閣學士，尋出為江西布政使。

translations.literal: After a year he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician and soon sent out as Jiangxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted to grand secretariat academician and shortly afterward posted as Jiangxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 殫心民事，值水災，行勘圩堤，落水致疾。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to the people's affairs; when flood came he went to inspect dikes and polders, fell into the water, and fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his full attention to civil affairs; during a flood he went out to survey dikes and polders, fell into the water, and took ill.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其勤，許解任養疴。

translations.literal: An edict praised his diligence and permitted him to leave office to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended his diligence and allowed him to resign and convalesce.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，特起授山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was specially recalled and appointed Shandong provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was specially summoned from retirement and appointed Shandong provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Jiangsu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 清介自矢，僮僕僅數人，出屏騶從，禁遊船聲伎，無事不許宴賓演劇。

translations.literal: He held himself to integrity and austerity, kept only a few servants, went out without runners and escorts, forbade pleasure boats and female entertainers, and allowed no banquets or theatrical performances unless there was official business.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged himself to frugal integrity, kept only a handful of servants, went abroad without runners or escorts, banned pleasure boats and singing girls, and permitted no feasts or plays except on official business.

sentences.zh: 吳下奢俗為之一變。

translations.literal: The extravagant customs of the Wu region were thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: The extravagant ways of the lower Yangtze were transformed by his example.

sentences.zh: 疏陳漕弊，略曰：「京漕積習相因，惟弊是營。

translations.literal: He memorialized on grain-transport abuses, saying in summary: 'Capital grain transport has long-standing practices handed down from age to age, and men pursue nothing but abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial on abuses in the grain transport he wrote, in summary: "Capital grain transport has entrenched customs passed down for generations, and everyone pursues nothing but graft.

sentences.zh: 米數之盈絀，米色之純雜，竟置不問。

translations.literal: Surplus or shortfall in grain quantities, purity or adulteration in grain quality—they leave these entirely unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the quantity of grain is ample or short, whether the grain is pure or adulterated—they pay no attention at all.

sentences.zh: 旗丁領運，無處不以米為挾制，即無處不以賄為通融。

translations.literal: When banner transport soldiers take charge of shipment, there is nowhere they do not use grain as leverage, and nowhere they do not use bribes to smooth matters.
translations.idiomatic: When banner transport soldiers take charge of the convoys, there is nowhere they do not use grain as leverage, and nowhere they do not use bribes to smooth the way.

sentences.zh: 推原其故，沿途之抑勒，由旗丁之有幫費；

translations.literal: Tracing the cause to its root, extortion along the route comes from the transport soldiers' having 'assistance fees';
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the matter to its root, the extortion along the route stems from the transport soldiers' demand for assistance fees;

sentences.zh: 旗丁之索幫費，由州縣之浮收。

translations.literal: the transport soldiers' demand for assistance fees comes from the prefectures' and counties' illegal surcharges.
translations.idiomatic: and the transport soldiers' demand for those fees stems from the illegal surcharges levied by prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 除弊當絕其源，嚴禁浮收，實絕弊源之首。

translations.literal: To eliminate abuses one must cut off the source; strictly forbidding illegal surcharges is truly the foremost way to sever the root of abuse.
translations.idiomatic: To eliminate abuses one must cut off the source; strictly forbidding illegal surcharges is truly the first step in severing the root of corruption.

sentences.zh: 請下有漕各省，列款指明，嚴行禁革，俾旗丁及漕運倉場，無從更生觀望冀幸之心。」

translations.literal: He requested that the grain-transport provinces be ordered to list items clearly and strictly prohibit and abolish them, so that transport soldiers and transport granaries would have no further occasion to harbor hopes of looking on and profiting by chance.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked that all grain-transport provinces be instructed to itemize each abuse clearly and enforce strict prohibition, so that transport soldiers and granary officials would no longer entertain hopes of profiting from the old ways."

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其實心除弊。

translations.literal: An edict praised his sincere effort to eliminate abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended his sincere effort to root out corruption.

sentences.zh: 常州知府胡觀瀾結交鹽政徵瑞長隨高柏林，派捐修葺江陰廣福寺。

translations.literal: Changzhou prefect Hu Guanlan associated with Salt Controller Zheng Rui and his chief attendant Gao Bolin and imposed levies to repair Jiangyin's Guangfu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guanlan, prefect of Changzhou, had cultivated ties with Zheng Rui, the salt controller, and his chief attendant Gao Bolin, and imposed levies to repair Guangfu Temple in Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 岳起疏言觀瀾、柏林雖罷逐，尚不足服眾心，請將錢二萬餘串責二人分償，以修蘇州官塘橋路。

translations.literal: Yue Qi memorialized that although Guanlan and Bolin had been dismissed and expelled, this was still insufficient to satisfy public sentiment; he asked that the more than twenty thousand strings of cash be charged to the two men to repay in shares, for repairing Suzhou's official roads and bridges.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi memorialized that although Guanlan and Bolin had been dismissed, this was still not enough to satisfy public opinion; he asked that the more than twenty thousand strings of cash be recovered from the two men in equal shares to repair Suzhou's official roads and bridges.

sentences.zh: 丹徒知縣黎誕登諷士紳臚其政績保留，實不職，劾罷之。

translations.literal: Dantu magistrate Li Yandeng had prompted gentry and scholars to enumerate his achievements for retention in office; in truth he was unfit for duty, and Yue Qi impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yandeng, magistrate of Dantu, had prompted local gentry to praise his record so he might be kept in office; finding him unfit for his post, Yue Qi impeached and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 五年，署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he acted as governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 劾南河工員莊剛、劉普等侵漁舞弊，莫澐於任所設店肆運貨至工居奇網利，並治如律。

translations.literal: He impeached Southern Canal engineering clerks Zhuang Gang, Liu Pu, and others for embezzlement and fraud; Mo Yun had set up shops at his post to transport goods to the works and corner the market for profit—all were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhuang Gang, Liu Pu, and other Southern Canal engineering officials for embezzlement and fraud; Mo Yun had opened shops at his post to ship goods to the worksites and profiteer by hoarding—all were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 揚州關溢額稅銀不入私，盡以報解；

translations.literal: Surplus tax silver at Yangzhou customs he did not take for himself but reported and remitted in full;
translations.idiomatic: Surplus tax silver at the Yangzhou customs he kept none of for himself but remitted in full;

sentences.zh: 覈減兩籓司耗羨閒款，實存銀數報部：並下部議行。

translations.literal: he audited and reduced miscellaneous surplus funds of the two provincial treasuries and reported actual silver on hand to the ministry—all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: he audited and cut the miscellaneous surplus funds of the two provincial treasuries and reported the actual silver on hand to the ministry—all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏請濬築毛城鋪以下河道堤岸、上游永城洪河、下游蕭、碭境內河堰，並藉帑舉工，分五年計畝徵還，允之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized requesting dredging and construction of river channels and dikes below Maochengpu, the upper Yongcheng Hong River, and lower Xia and Dang interior river dikes, borrowing treasury funds to undertake the work and recovering it over five years by assessment per mu—all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he memorialized to dredge and build the river channels and dikes below Maochengpu, the upper Yongcheng Hong River, and the interior river dikes in Xia and Dang, borrowing treasury funds for the work and recovering the cost over five years by assessment per mu of land—the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，入覲，以疾留京，署禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he came to audience, remained in the capital on account of illness, and acted as vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he came to court, remained in the capital because of illness, and served as acting vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會孝淑皇后奉移山陵，坐會疏措語不經，革職留任。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaoshu was moved to the imperial tomb, he was punished for improper wording in a joint memorial and was stripped of office but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiaoshu was moved to the imperial tomb, he was punished because a joint memorial he signed used improper language; he was stripped of rank but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 尋命解署職，遂卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to relinquish his acting post and then died.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered to relinquish his acting appointment, and he died.

sentences.zh: 帝深惜之，贈太子少保，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted his loss, posthumously granted him Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bestowed condolence gifts according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned his loss, posthumously granted him the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and bestowed condolence gifts according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔問其家產，僅屋四間、田七十六畝。

translations.literal: He had no son; an edict inquired into his household property—only four rooms and seventy-six mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; the throne ordered an inquiry into his estate and found only four rooms and seventy-six mu of land.

sentences.zh: 故事，旗員歿無嗣者產入官。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a banner official died without heirs his property entered the state.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a banner official died without heirs his property reverted to the state.

sentences.zh: 以岳起家清貧，留贍其妻；

translations.literal: Because Yue Qi's family had been upright and poor, the property was left to support his wife;
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue Qi's household had been upright and poor, the estate was left to support his wife;

sentences.zh: 妻歿，官為管業，以為祭掃修墳之資。

translations.literal: when she died the government managed the estate as funds for sacrifices, tomb sweeping, and grave repair.
translations.idiomatic: when she died the government took charge of the property to provide for sacrifices, tomb sweeping, and grave maintenance.

sentences.zh: 異數也。

translations.literal: This was an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Such favor was unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 妻亦嚴正，岳起為巡撫時，一日親往籍畢沅家。

translations.literal: His wife was also stern and upright; when Yue Qi was governor he went in person one day to inventory Bi Yuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was equally stern and upright; while Yue Qi was governor he went in person one day to inventory the household of Bi Yuan.

sentences.zh: 暮歸，飲酒微醺。

translations.literal: Returning at dusk, he drank wine and became slightly tipsy.
translations.idiomatic: He returned at dusk slightly tipsy from wine.

sentences.zh: 妻正色曰：「畢公躭於酒色，不保其家，君方畏戒之不暇，乃復效彼耶？」

translations.literal: His wife said sternly: 'Master Bi was addicted to wine and women and could not preserve his household; you are still busy fearing and guarding against this—will you now imitate him?'
translations.idiomatic: His wife said sternly, "Master Bi was lost to wine and women and could not preserve his household; you are still busy guarding yourself against such ruin—will you now imitate him?"

sentences.zh: 岳起謝之。

translations.literal: Yue Qi apologized to her.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Qi apologized to her.

sentences.zh: 及至京，居無邸舍，病歿於僧寺，妻紡績以終。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he had no residence; ill, he died in a Buddhist temple, and his wife supported herself by spinning to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he had no house of his own; he fell ill and died in a Buddhist temple, and his wife lived out her days by spinning.

sentences.zh: 吳民尤思其德，呼曰岳青天，演為歌謠，謂可繼湯斌雲。

translations.literal: The people of Wu especially remembered his virtue, calling him 'Yue the Blue Heaven,' turning this into ballads, and saying he could succeed Tang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu cherished his memory above all, calling him "Yue the Blue Heaven," setting his praise to song, and saying he could stand in the line of Tang Bin.

sentences.zh: 荊道乾，字健中，山西臨晉人。

translations.literal: Jing Daoqian, style name Jianzhong, was a native of Linjin, Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Daoqian, whose style was Jianzhong, came from Linjin in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十四年舉人，大挑知縣，官湖南，歷麻陽、龍山、東安、永順、慈利、靖州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong he became a provincial graduate, was selected in the great assignment as magistrate, served in Hunan, and successively held Mayang, Longshan, Dong'an, Yongshun, Cili, and Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examinations, was selected in the great assignment as magistrate, served in Hunan, and held office in Mayang, Longshan, Dong'an, Yongshun, Cili, and Jingzhou in turn.

sentences.zh: 所至有惠政，屏陋規，平冤獄。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he had benevolent administration, abolished petty abuses, and righted wrongful cases.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he brought benevolent rule, abolished petty abuses, and righted wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 在靖州賑饑，尤多全活，屢膺上考。

translations.literal: At Jingzhou he relieved famine and especially saved many lives; he repeatedly received top evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou he relieved famine and saved countless lives; he repeatedly received top evaluations from the throne.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，遷甘肅寧夏同知，入覲，大學士劉墉曾官湖南巡撫，稱之曰：「第一清官也。」

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to be Ningxia subprefect in Gansu; coming to audience, Grand Secretary Liu Yong, who had once been Hunan governor, said of him: 'The foremost incorrupt official.'
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to be subprefect of Ningxia in Gansu; when he came to court, Grand Secretary Liu Yong, who had once served as Hunan governor, said of him, "The foremost incorrupt official."

sentences.zh: 名始著。

translations.literal: His reputation then became established.
translations.idiomatic: His fame was established from that day.

sentences.zh: 尋署石峰堡同知，時方用兵，治事不廢，修復水利，复薦卓異記名。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as Shifeng Fort subprefect; war was then underway, yet he did not neglect administration, restored waterworks, and was again recommended as outstanding and placed on the promotion list.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as acting subprefect of Shifeng Fort; though war was underway he did not neglect his duties, restored irrigation works, and was again recommended as outstanding and placed on the promotion list.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，擢安徽池州知府，屢署徽寧池太道，筦蕪湖關，贏餘不入己，以充賑恤。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to Anhui Chizhou prefect, repeatedly acted as Huaining-Chizhou-Taiping intendant, managed Wuhu customs, kept no surplus for himself, and used it for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was promoted to prefect of Chizhou in Anhui, repeatedly acted as intendant of Huizhou, Ningguo, Chizhou, and Taiping, managed the Wuhu customs house, kept none of the surplus for himself, and devoted it to famine relief.

sentences.zh: 調安慶，硃珪為巡撫，尤信任之，疏薦，擢山東登萊青道，攝布政使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Anqing, Zhu Gui was governor and especially trusted him, memorialized recommending him, and he was promoted to Shandong Dengzhou-Laizhou-Qingzhou circuit intendant and acted as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Anqing, where Governor Zhu Gui especially trusted him and memorialized in his favor, he was promoted to intendant of Dengzhou, Laizhou, and Qingzhou in Shandong and acted as provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以激濁揚清為己任，薦廉吏崔映淮、李如珩等，而劾不飭者。

translations.literal: He took stirring the muddy and raising the clear as his duty, recommended incorrupt officials Cui Yinghuai, Li Ruheng, and others, and impeached the undisciplined.
translations.idiomatic: He made it his mission to purge corruption and elevate the upright, recommending honest officials such as Cui Yinghuai and Li Ruheng while impeaching the undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he was transferred to provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiaqing he was appointed provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Jiangsu provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Jiangsu provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是州縣存留俸薪役食及驛站經費，改解籓庫，俟奏銷後請支，始則防吏侵挪，久之解有浮費，發有短平。

translations.literal: Previously prefectures and counties retained salaries, runner provisions, and courier-station funds but were required to remit them to the provincial treasury and request disbursement only after memorialized settlement; at first this was to prevent clerks' embezzlement, but in time remittance had illegal surcharges and disbursement had short weights.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the salaries, runner provisions, and courier-station funds retained by prefectures and counties had been remitted to the provincial treasury and disbursed only after memorialized settlement; this was meant to prevent clerks from embezzling funds, but over time remittance came with illegal surcharges and disbursement with short weights.

sentences.zh: 或勒抵前官虧空，佐雜教官不能得俸，驛傳領於臬司；

translations.literal: Some were forced to cover predecessors' deficits; assistant instructors and miscellaneous educational officials could not receive salaries; courier service was managed by the provincial judge;
translations.idiomatic: Some funds were seized to cover predecessors' deficits; assistant instructors and minor educational officials went unpaid; courier service fell under the provincial judge;

sentences.zh: 或苛駁案牘，因索餽遺，郵政日弛廢。

translations.literal: some harshly rejected documents and thereby extorted gifts, and the postal system daily fell into decay.
translations.idiomatic: others harshly rejected documents to extort gifts, and the postal system fell ever further into decay.

sentences.zh: 道乾入覲時，面陳其弊，請悉依定章，於州縣徵收時開支，省解領之繁。

translations.literal: When Daoqian came to audience he stated these abuses in person and asked that all follow the established regulations, disbursing at the time of collection by prefectures and counties, to spare the trouble of remitting and receiving.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Daoqian came to court he stated these abuses in person and asked that disbursement follow the established regulations at the time of collection by prefectures and counties, sparing the trouble of remittance and requisition.

sentences.zh: 仁宗俞可；

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor approved;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong approved;

sentences.zh: 至是疏上施行，天下便之。

translations.literal: at this time he memorialized and it was implemented, and the empire found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: he now memorialized and the reform was implemented, to the benefit of the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 上方欲整飭漕政，以巡撫岳起及道乾皆有清名，責其肅清諸弊。

translations.literal: The court then wished to rectify grain transport; because Governor Yue Qi and Daoqian both had reputations for integrity, it charged them to purge all abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The court wished to reform grain transport; because Governor Yue Qi and Jing Daoqian both enjoyed reputations for integrity, it charged them to purge all abuses.

sentences.zh: 到官三閱月，擢安徽巡撫，疏請禁徵漕浮收舊耗米一斗，給運丁五升，加給二升。

translations.literal: Three months after taking office he was promoted to Anhui governor; he memorialized requesting prohibition of illegal surcharges on grain transport, the old practice of one dou of wastage rice, giving transport soldiers five sheng, with an additional two sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Three months after taking office he was promoted to governor of Anhui; he memorialized to forbid illegal surcharges on grain transport, including the old wastage levy of one dou per unit, granting transport soldiers five sheng with an additional two sheng.

sentences.zh: 運丁所得，有據可考；

translations.literal: What the transport soldiers received had documentary basis for verification;
translations.idiomatic: What the transport soldiers received could be verified by clear records;

sentences.zh: 其所用沿途浮費，採訪知之，應禁革。

translations.literal: the illegal surcharges they used along the route he learned through investigation and they should be prohibited and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: the illegal surcharges they collected along the route he had learned through investigation and should be prohibited and abolished.

sentences.zh: 詔下所奏於有漕各省永禁。

translations.literal: An edict transmitted his memorial to all grain-transport provinces for permanent prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his proposals permanently enforced in all grain-transport provinces.

sentences.zh: 又言：「屯田所以贍運，每丁派田若干及應得租耔，新僉旗丁不能了然。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Garrison fields exist to support transport; how much land is assigned to each soldier and what rent grain is due—the newly enrolled banner transport soldiers cannot understand this clearly.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Garrison fields exist to support transport, yet how much land is assigned to each soldier and what rent grain is due—the newly enrolled banner transport soldiers cannot make sense of it.

sentences.zh: 令糧道刊刻木榜，俾僉丁認田收租。

translations.literal: He ordered the grain intendant to carve wooden placards so enrolled soldiers could identify fields and collect rent.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the grain intendant to publish wooden placards so enrolled soldiers could identify their fields and collect rent.

sentences.zh: 運船領款，刻易知單，由丁正身親領，以杜包領欺壓之弊。

translations.literal: For transport boats receiving funds, he had simple receipts carved so soldiers received payment in person, to stop the abuse of proxy collection and oppression.
translations.idiomatic: For funds paid to transport boats he had plain receipts printed so soldiers collected payment in person, to stop proxy collection and intimidation.

sentences.zh: 田冊歸糧道收管，另造副冊發各衛以備查驗。」

translations.literal: Field registers were kept by the grain intendant, and duplicate registers were made and sent to each garrison for inspection.'
translations.idiomatic: Field registers were kept by the grain intendant, with duplicate copies sent to each garrison for inspection."

sentences.zh: 並允行。

translations.literal: All was approved for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved for implementation.

sentences.zh: 宿州、靈壁、泗州水災，道乾親往監視賑廠。

translations.literal: Suzhou, Lingbi, and Sizhou suffered flood; Daoqian went in person to supervise relief stations.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhou (Anhui), Lingbi, and Sizhou suffered floods, Jing Daoqian went in person to supervise the relief stations.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞罷，詔許解任調理，俟病痊來京候簡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on grounds of illness he requested retirement; an edict permitted him to leave office to recuperate and, when recovered, to come to the capital awaiting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the throne permitted him to leave office to recuperate and, when recovered, to come to the capital awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 次年三月，詔詢道乾病狀，已先卒於安慶，帝悼惜，賜祭，賜其孫炆舉人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year an edict inquired after Daoqian's illness; he had already died at Anqing; the emperor mourned him, granted sacrificial rites, and granted his grandson Wen the status of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year an edict inquired after his health; he had already died at Anqing; the emperor mourned his loss, granted sacrificial rites, and conferred provincial graduate status on his grandson Wen.

sentences.zh: 道乾由監司不三年擢至巡撫，求治益急，不避嫌怨，自處刻苦。

translations.literal: Daoqian rose from surveillance commissioner to governor in less than three years, sought governance ever more urgently, did not avoid resentment, and treated himself with austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Daoqian had risen from surveillance commissioner to governor in less than three years; he pursued reform ever more urgently, shrank from no enmity, and lived in austere self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 臨歿，呼舊僚至寢所，指床下金示之曰：「吾受重恩，積養廉數千兩，足以歸喪。

translations.literal: Near death he summoned former colleagues to his bedchamber, pointed to gold beneath the bed, and showed them, saying: 'I have received great favor and saved several thousand taels of integrity stipend—enough to return my body home.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he summoned former colleagues to his bedside, pointed to gold beneath the bed, and said, "I have received great favor from the throne and saved several thousand taels of my integrity stipend—enough to bring my body home.

sentences.zh: 諸君素愛我，勿為斂賻。」

translations.literal: You have always loved me—do not collect funeral contributions for me.'
translations.idiomatic: You have always been fond of me—do not collect funeral contributions on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 又呼其兄曰：「兄仁弱，勿聽人慫恿受賻，違吾意。」

translations.literal: He also called his elder brother and said: 'Elder brother, you are benevolent but weak—do not listen to others who urge you to accept contributions, going against my wish.'
translations.idiomatic: He also called his elder brother and said, "Brother, you are kind but weak—do not let anyone persuade you to accept contributions against my wish."

sentences.zh: 兄如其言。

translations.literal: His brother did as he said.
translations.idiomatic: His brother did as he asked.

sentences.zh: 謝啟昆，字蘊山，江西南康人。

translations.literal: Xie Qikun, style name Yunshan, was a native of Nankang, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qikun, whose style was Yunshan, came from Nankang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年進士，朝考第一，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong, a metropolitan graduate, first in the palace examination, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong he became a metropolitan graduate, ranked first in the court examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典河南鄉試，分校禮闈，均得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Henan provincial examination and served on the metropolitan examination board—both produced worthy graduates.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Henan provincial examination and served on the metropolitan examination board; both produced worthy graduates.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，出為江蘇鎮江知府，調揚州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he went out as Jiangsu Zhenjiang prefect and was transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was posted as prefect of Zhenjiang in Jiangsu and then transferred to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明於吏事，所持堅正，上官異意不為奪。

translations.literal: He was skilled in administrative affairs, held firm and upright principles, and was not swayed when superiors disagreed.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in administration, held firm and upright principles, and was not swayed when superiors disagreed.

sentences.zh: 治東台徐述夔詩詞悖逆獄遲緩，褫職戍軍台。

translations.literal: In handling the Dongtai Xu Shukui treason-by-poetry case he was slow; he was stripped of office and banished to serve at a military garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office and banished to a military garrison for proceeding too slowly in the Dongtai treason case involving Xu Shukui's poetry.

sentences.zh: 尋捐復原官，留江南。

translations.literal: Soon he purchased restoration of his former rank and remained in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon purchased restoration of his former rank and remained in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父憂，奪情署安徽寧國知府；

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he was recalled from mourning to act as Anhui Ningguo prefect;
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he was recalled from mourning to serve as acting prefect of Ningguo in Anhui;

sentences.zh: 复遭母憂，服闋，稱病久不出。

translations.literal: he again suffered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he claimed illness and long did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: he mourned his mother as well; when mourning ended he claimed illness and long declined to take office.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，特擢江南河庫道，遷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he was specially promoted to Jiangnan river-treasury intendant and transferred to Zhejiang provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year he was specially promoted to Jiangnan river-treasury intendant and appointed Zhejiang provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was appointed Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 州縣倉庫積虧八十餘萬，不一歲悉補完。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county treasuries had accumulated deficits of more than eight hundred thousand; in less than a year he made them all good.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county treasuries had accumulated deficits of more than eight hundred thousand taels; in less than a year he made them all good.

sentences.zh: 高宗異其才，以浙江財賦地虧尤多，特調任。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor marveled at his talent; because Zhejiang's revenues and levies had especially large deficits, he was specially transferred there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong marveled at his talent; because Zhejiang's revenue deficits were especially large, he was specially transferred there.

sentences.zh: 歷三歲，亦彌補十之五。

translations.literal: Over three years he likewise made good five-tenths of the deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years he likewise made good half the deficits.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，擢廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to Guangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 上疏，略曰：「各省倉庫積弊有三變。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying in summary: "The accumulated abuses of provincial treasuries have three stages of change.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, saying in summary: "The accumulated abuses of provincial treasuries have three stages of change.

sentences.zh: 始則大吏貪婪者利州縣之餽賂，僨事者資州縣之攤賠。

translations.literal: At first greedy high officials profited from prefectural and county bribes, while those who had run up debts drew on prefectures and counties for shared indemnities.
translations.idiomatic: At first greedy high officials profited from prefectural and county bribes, while those who had run up debts drew on prefectures and counties for shared indemnities.

sentences.zh: 州縣匿其私橐，以公帑應之，離任則虧空累累。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties hid their private purses and met obligations from public funds; on leaving office deficits piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties hid their private funds and met obligations from public treasuries; on leaving office deficits piled up.

sentences.zh: 大吏既餌其資助，不得不抑勒後任接收。

translations.literal: Once high officials had taken their subsidies, they had no choice but to pressure successors into accepting the deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Once high officials had taken their subsidies, they had no choice but to pressure successors into accepting the deficits.

sentences.zh: 此虧空之緣起也。

translations.literal: This is how deficits arose.
translations.idiomatic: This is how deficits arose.

sentences.zh: 繼則大吏庸闇者任其欺矇，姑息者又懼興大獄，以敢接虧空為能員，以禀揭虧空為多事。

translations.literal: Next, mediocre and obtuse high officials let themselves be deceived, while indulgent ones feared stirring up major cases, treating willingness to accept deficits as competence and memorials exposing deficits as meddling.
translations.idiomatic: Next, mediocre and obtuse high officials let themselves be deceived, while indulgent ones feared stirring up major cases, treating willingness to accept deficits as competence and memorials exposing deficits as meddling.

sentences.zh: 州縣且有藉多虧挾制上司升遷美缺者。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties even used large deficits to coerce superiors into granting promotion to prized posts.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties even used large deficits to coerce superiors into granting promotion to prized posts.

sentences.zh: 此虧空之濫觴也。

translations.literal: This is how deficits spread unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: This is how deficits spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 近年不職督撫相繼敗露，諸大吏共相濯磨，州縣亦爭先彌補。

translations.literal: In recent years incompetent governors-general and governors have been exposed one after another; the high officials have all polished one another, and prefectures and counties have also rushed to make deficits good.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years incompetent governors-general and governors have been exposed one after another; the high officials have all striven to reform themselves, and prefectures and counties have also rushed to make deficits good.

sentences.zh: 但彌補之法，寬則生玩，胥吏因緣為奸；

translations.literal: But in methods of making deficits good, leniency breeds laxity and clerks seize the chance for corruption;
translations.idiomatic: But in methods of making deficits good, leniency breeds laxity and clerks seize the chance for corruption;

sentences.zh: 急則張皇，百姓先受其累。

translations.literal: haste breeds alarm, and the common people suffer first.
translations.idiomatic: haste breeds alarm, and the common people suffer first.

sentences.zh: 各省貧富不同，難易迥別，一法立即一弊生，惟在因地制宜。

translations.literal: The provinces differ in wealth and poverty and in ease and difficulty; one rule applied at once produces one new abuse—the only course is to suit measures to local conditions.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces differ in wealth and poverty and in ease and difficulty; one rule applied at once produces one new abuse—the only course is to suit measures to local conditions.

sentences.zh: 率定章程，又多窒礙。

translations.literal: To impose uniform regulations is again full of obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: To impose uniform regulations is again full of obstacles.

sentences.zh: 請飭下各省先查實虧之數、原虧之人，如律論治。

translations.literal: I ask that orders be sent to every province first to verify the amount of actual deficits and the persons originally responsible, and to punish them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that orders be sent to every province first to verify the amount of actual deficits and the persons originally responsible, and to punish them according to law.

sentences.zh: 其無著者，詳記檔案，使猾吏無可影射。

translations.literal: Where there is no one to hold accountable, let it be recorded in detail in the files so that crafty clerks have nothing to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is no one to hold accountable, let it be recorded in detail in the files so that crafty clerks have nothing to exploit.

sentences.zh: 多分年限，使後任量力補苴，不必展轉株求，亦不必程功旦夕。

translations.literal: Spread repayment over more years, letting successors make good deficits according to their capacity, without endless pursuit through successive offices and without demanding completion overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Spread repayment over more years, letting successors make good deficits according to their capacity, without endless pursuit through successive offices and without demanding completion overnight.

sentences.zh: 責成督撫裁陋規以清其源，倡節儉以絕其流，講求愛民之術以培元氣，獎擢清廉之員以勵官常。

translations.literal: Hold governors-general and governors responsible for cutting abusive customs to clear the source, promote frugality to stop the flow, seek methods that cherish the people to nurture vital strength, and reward and promote incorrupt officials to uphold official norms.
translations.idiomatic: Hold governors-general and governors responsible for cutting abusive customs to clear the source, promote frugality to stop the flow, seek methods that cherish the people to nurture vital strength, and reward and promote incorrupt officials to uphold official norms.

sentences.zh: 日計不足，月計有餘。

translations.literal: Day by day the account falls short; month by month it comes out ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day the account falls short; month by month it comes out ahead.

sentences.zh: 不數年間，休養生息，不徒倉庫充盈，吏治民生亦蒸蒸日上。

translations.literal: Within a few years, through rest and recovery, not only will the treasuries be full, but official governance and the people's livelihood will also rise steadily.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years, through rest and recovery, not only will the treasuries be full, but official governance and the people's livelihood will also rise steadily.

sentences.zh: 廣西自孫士毅經營安南，軍需供億，所費不貲，米銀裝械，毀棄關外，令州縣分賠，遂致通省皆虧。

translations.literal: Guangxi, since Sun Shiyi managed Annam, had military supplies in vast quantities at enormous cost; grain, silver, and equipment were abandoned beyond the passes, and prefectures and counties were ordered to share indemnities, so that the whole province fell into deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi, since Sun Shiyi managed Annam, had military supplies in vast quantities at enormous cost; grain, silver, and equipment were abandoned beyond the passes, and prefectures and counties were ordered to share indemnities, so that the whole province fell into deficit.

sentences.zh: 本非州縣侵蝕，且人已去任，接收者正在補苴，一經參追，難保不勸捐派累。

translations.literal: This was not embezzlement by prefectures and counties; moreover the men had already left office, and those receiving the posts were just making deficits good—once impeachment and pursuit began, it was hard to ensure that there would not be forced contributions and levies on the people.
translations.idiomatic: This was not embezzlement by prefectures and counties; moreover the men had already left office, and those receiving the posts were just making deficits good—once impeachment and pursuit began, it was hard to ensure that there would not be forced contributions and levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 惟率司、道、府、州省衣節食，革去一切陋規，俾州縣從容彌補，進廉去貪，無累百姓，計三年之內，庫項必可補足。

translations.literal: Only if the provincial, circuit, prefectural, and department officials lead by wearing plain clothes and eating sparingly, abolish all abusive customs, let prefectures and counties make deficits good at a measured pace, advance the incorrupt and remove the greedy without burdening the people, can the treasury shortfalls be made good within three years.
translations.idiomatic: Only if the provincial, circuit, prefectural, and department officials lead by wearing plain clothes and eating sparingly, abolish all abusive customs, let prefectures and counties make deficits good at a measured pace, advance the incorrupt and remove the greedy without burdening the people, can the treasury shortfalls be made good within three years.

sentences.zh: 惟是數十人補之而不足，一二人敗之而有餘。

translations.literal: Yet dozens may make good deficits and still fall short, while one or two may ruin them and leave a surplus of harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet dozens may make good deficits and still fall short, while one or two may ruin them and leave a surplus of harm.

sentences.zh: 是又在知人善任，大法小廉，不愛逢迎，不存姑息，庶不致後有續虧之患。」

translations.literal: This again depends on knowing men and assigning them well, on strict law and modest integrity, on not courting flattery, and on not indulgence, so that later there may not be the calamity of renewed deficits."
translations.idiomatic: This again depends on knowing men and assigning them well, on strict law and modest integrity, on not courting flattery, and on not indulgence, so that later there may not be the calamity of renewed deficits."

sentences.zh: 又言：「彌補虧空，初不為一身免累之計，乃有實際。

translations.literal: He also said: "Making deficits good is not at first a plan to spare oneself from liability; it must have practical effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Making deficits good is not at first a plan to spare oneself from liability; it must have practical effect.

sentences.zh: 臣前歷山西、浙江，皆未諮部，亦未諮追原籍。

translations.literal: When I previously served in Shanxi and Zhejiang, I never consulted the ministry, nor did I pursue men to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: When I previously served in Shanxi and Zhejiang, I never consulted the ministry, nor did I pursue men to their native places.

sentences.zh: 蓋當日之員，大半死亡遣戍，子孫貧乏者多，諮追徒滋紛擾，如數完繳者實無二三，現任反置身事外。

translations.literal: For the officials of those days had mostly died or been banished to garrison service; many of their descendants were poor; pursuit by consultation only bred disorder, and those who actually paid in full were scarcely two or three, while incumbents were left outside the matter.
translations.idiomatic: For the officials of those days had mostly died or been banished to garrison service; many of their descendants were poor; pursuit by consultation only bred disorder, and those who actually paid in full were scarcely two or three, while incumbents were left outside the matter.

sentences.zh: 廣西庫項未完者三十九州縣，覈其廉數多寡，分限三年，按月交庫，於交代時有不足者，即以虧空論劾。」

translations.literal: In Guangxi thirty-nine prefectures and counties still had unfinished treasury accounts; I have verified the amounts of their deficits, set a three-year limit, required monthly payment into the treasury, and where there is shortfall at handover of office, I will impeach it as deficit."
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi thirty-nine prefectures and counties still had unfinished treasury accounts; I have verified the amounts of their deficits, set a three-year limit, required monthly payment into the treasury, and where there is shortfall at handover of office, I will impeach it as deficit."

sentences.zh: 疏入，仁宗嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Emperor Renzong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Renzong praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 時詔買補倉穀，取諸豐稔鄰縣，禁於本境採買。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered purchase of grain to replenish granaries, taking it from neighboring counties with abundant harvests and forbidding procurement within one's own jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict ordered purchase of grain to replenish granaries, taking it from neighboring counties with abundant harvests and forbidding procurement within one's own jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 啟昆言廣西跬步皆山，轉運不減於穀價，恐不肖者因採買之難，或為勒派，請仍聽本境買補便，詔如所議。

translations.literal: Qikun said that in Guangxi every short step is over mountains, and transport costs are no less than the price of grain; he feared that unscrupulous men, because procurement was difficult, might resort to forced levies, and asked that local procurement within the jurisdiction still be permitted for convenience; an edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Qikun said that in Guangxi every short step is over mountains, and transport costs are no less than the price of grain; he feared that unscrupulous men, because procurement was difficult, might resort to forced levies, and asked that local procurement within the jurisdiction still be permitted for convenience; an edict followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 廣西土司四十有六，生計日絀，貸於客民，輒以田產準折。

translations.literal: Guangxi had forty-six native chieftaincies; their livelihoods daily grew strained; they borrowed from settler commoners and invariably pledged fields in settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi had forty-six native chieftaincies whose livelihoods grew ever more strained; they borrowed from Han settlers and invariably pledged their fields in settlement.

sentences.zh: 啟昆請禁重利盤剝，違者治罪。

translations.literal: Qikun requested prohibition of usurious exploitation; violators were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qikun requested a ban on usurious exploitation, with violators punished by law.

sentences.zh: 田產給還土司，其無力回贖者，俟收田租滿一本一利，田歸原主，五年為斷；

translations.literal: Fields were returned to the chieftains; those unable to redeem waited until field rent collected equaled principal plus interest, then the fields returned to the original owners, with five years as the limit;
translations.idiomatic: Fields were returned to the chieftains; those unable to redeem immediately would regain their land once rent collected equaled principal plus interest, with five years as the limit;

sentences.zh: 其不禁客民入苗地者，廉土民馴愚，物產稀少，藉販運以通有無也。

translations.literal: As for his not prohibiting settler commoners from entering Miao territory, [it was because] he considered the native people simple and docile, local products were scarce, and they relied on transport trade to exchange what they had and lacked.
translations.idiomatic: He did not bar Han settlers from entering Miao territory because he judged the natives simple and tractable, local products were scarce, and commerce was needed to circulate goods.

sentences.zh: 仿浙江海塘竹簍囊石之法，修築興安陡河石堤，以除水患。

translations.literal: Following the Zhejiang seacoast method of bamboo baskets packed with stone, he built the Xing'an Steep River stone dike to eliminate flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting the Zhejiang seacoast practice of stone packed in bamboo baskets, he built the Xing'an Steep River stone dike to end the flood hazard.

sentences.zh: 河流深通，舊銅船過陡河必一月，至是三日而畢。

translations.literal: The river ran deep and clear; formerly copper transport boats required a month to pass Steep River; at this time it was finished in three days.
translations.idiomatic: Once the channel ran deep and clear, copper transport boats that had needed a month to pass Steep River now completed the passage in three days.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒於官，詔嘉其廉潔，於所節省潯、梧兩關盈餘項下賜銀三千兩治喪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in office; an edict praised his integrity and frugality and granted three thousand taels from the surplus saved at the Xun and Wu passes for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died in office. The throne praised his integrity and granted three thousand taels from the surplus he had saved at the Xun and Wu customs posts toward his funeral.

sentences.zh: 廣西士民請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Guangxi gentry and commoners requested his enshrinement in the temple of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: The gentry and people of Guangxi asked that he be enshrined in the local temple of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 啟昆少以文學名，博聞強識，尤善為詩。

translations.literal: Qikun was famed from youth for letters, was broadly learned with a strong memory, and was especially skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qikun won early fame for his literary attainments, possessed broad learning and a formidable memory, and was especially accomplished as a poet.

sentences.zh: 著《樹經堂集》、《西魏書》、《小學考》，晚成《廣西通志》，為世所稱。

translations.literal: He authored the Shujingtang Collection, the History of the Western Wei, and the Study of Elementary Learning; late in life he completed the Guangxi General Gazetteer, all praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Shujingtang Collection, the History of the Western Wei, and the Study of Elementary Learning, and late in life finished the Guangxi General Gazetteer, works widely admired in his day.

sentences.zh: 李殿圖，字桓符，直隸高陽人。

translations.literal: Li Diantu, style name Huanfu, was a native of Gaoyang, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Diantu, whose style was Huanfu, came from Gaoyang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he became a metropolitan graduate, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 典湖南鄉試，遷御史。

translations.literal: He presided over the Hunan provincial examination and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Hunan provincial examination and was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 督廣西學政，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He supervised Guangxi education and was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Guangxi education intendant and was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，甘肅回亂，從阿桂、福康安赴軍治糧餉、台站，授鞏秦階道。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, during the Gansu Muslim rebellion, he followed Agui and Fuk'anggan to the army to manage provisions and courier stations and was appointed intendant of Gong, Qin, and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year, when the Gansu Muslim rebellion broke out, he followed Agui and Fuk'anggan to the front to manage grain funds and courier stations and was appointed intendant of Gong, Qin, and Jie.

sentences.zh: 軍事初竣，民、回相仇，焚掠報復，訛言時起。

translations.literal: When military affairs had just concluded, Han and Muslim communities were mutually hostile; burning, plunder, and revenge followed, and false rumors arose from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: As the campaign wound down, Han and Muslim communities were at odds; arson, looting, and reprisals spread, and rumors constantly flared.

sentences.zh: 殿圖處以鎮靜，叛黨緣坐，婦稚量情釋宥；

translations.literal: Diantu handled matters with calm; rebel parties were implicated by association, and women and children were released according to circumstances;
translations.idiomatic: Diantu responded with calm; where rebel factions were implicated by association, he released women and children as circumstances warranted;

sentences.zh: 罹害戶口，隨宜賑恤，流亡漸安。

translations.literal: households that had suffered harm were relieved according to need, and exiles gradually grew tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: households that had suffered harm received relief as needed, and displaced people gradually settled down.

sentences.zh: 卓泥土司與四川松潘、漳臘各番爭噶噶固山界，殿圖輕騎履勘，歷小洮河、丈八嶺、鸚哥口，皆人跡罕到，群番導行，片語判決，立石達魚山頂而還。

translations.literal: The Zhuotu native chieftain disputed the boundary of Gagagu Mountain with the Songpan and Zhangla tribes of Sichuan; Diantu went on light horse to survey on foot, passing the Little Tao River, Zhangba Ridge, and Parrot Pass—all rarely visited by human tracks—with the tribes guiding the way; a few words settled the judgment, and he set up a stone on Dayu Mountain summit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuotu chieftain disputed the boundary of Gagagu Mountain with the Songpan and Zhangla tribes of Sichuan. Diantu rode out lightly to survey on foot, crossing the Little Tao River, Zhangba Ridge, and Parrot Pass—places scarcely touched by travelers—with tribal guides; he settled the dispute in a few words, erected a boundary stone atop Dayu Mountain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 高宗幾餘考涇、渭清濁源流，命殿圖親勘，自秦州溯流至鳥鼠、崆峒，繪圖附說以進，詔嘉其詳實。

translations.literal: In his leisure the Gaozong Emperor studied the clear and turbid sources of the Jing and Wei rivers and ordered Diantu to inspect in person; from Qinzhou he went upstream to Bird-and-Rat and Kongtong, submitted maps with explanations, and the edict praised their detail and solidity.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure Emperor Gaozong studied whether the Jing and Wei were clear or turbid at their sources and ordered Diantu to inspect them in person. From Qinzhou he traced the rivers upstream to Bird-and-Rat and Kongtong, submitted maps with explanatory notes, and the throne praised their thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 六十年，遷福建按察使，嘉慶三年，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was transferred to Fujian provincial judge; in the third year of Jiaqing he was promoted in place to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year he was appointed Fujian provincial judge, and in the third year of Jiaqing he was promoted in place to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「乾隆中，業農家必畜騾馬三四以任耕種，嗣後官吏借用應差，漸形滋擾，應嚴行革除。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'In the Qianlong period farming households necessarily kept three or four mules and horses for plowing; afterward officials borrowed them for corvée service and harassment gradually grew; this should be strictly abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: 'Under Qianlong, farming households routinely kept three or four mules and horses for cultivation. Later officials borrowed them for corvée duty, and abuse gradually spread; this practice should be abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 獄訟必速為審結，開釋無辜，小民始得安業。

translations.literal: Litigation must be swiftly tried and concluded; releasing the innocent allows the common people to settle to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Cases must be heard and concluded promptly; only by releasing the innocent can ordinary people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 常平倉穀積久弊生，民未受益，官倉已受其虧。

translations.literal: Ever-normal granary grain, long stored, breeds abuses; the people do not benefit while the official granaries already suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: Grain in the ever-normal granaries, stored too long, breeds corruption: the people gain nothing while the public stores already take the loss.

sentences.zh: 無災之年，不宜貸假。

translations.literal: In years without disaster, loans should not be made.
translations.idiomatic: In years without disaster, grain should not be lent out.

sentences.zh: 吏役例有定額，近則人思託足，藉免役徭。

translations.literal: Clerks and runners have fixed quotas, but recently people seek a foothold and use this to avoid corvée and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and runners have fixed quotas, yet lately men seek posts under them to escape corvée and tax service.

sentences.zh: 關津稅口，官署長隨，呼朋引類，並為奸藪，宜並禁止。」

translations.literal: At tax barriers and passes, officials' chief attendants call in companions and all become nests of villainy; these too should be prohibited together.'
translations.idiomatic: At customs posts and ferry tolls, magistrates' chief attendants gather cronies and turn the places into dens of fraud; these abuses should be banned as well.'

sentences.zh: 詔下直省一體察禁。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all provinces alike to investigate and prohibit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered every province to investigate and enforce the ban.

sentences.zh: 閩俗售田，田面田根，糾纏不決。

translations.literal: Fujian custom in selling fields distinguishes surface rights and root rights, and disputes drag on unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian, land sales distinguish surface rights from root tenure, and disputes often remain unsettled.

sentences.zh: 蠹吏影射，佃戶頑抗，錢糧日多脫欠，徵收不敷，每以虛出通關而致虧缺，殿圖奏請嚴治。

translations.literal: Corrupt clerks used shadow registration; tenants stubbornly resisted; grain levies daily fell short in collection; because fictitious clearance was issued to pass inspection, deficits resulted; Diantu memorialized requesting strict punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks falsified records, tenants defied payment, and tax collections fell ever further short; officials papered over shortfalls with false clearances, deepening the deficit. Diantu memorialized for stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 在任逾年，庫儲大增。

translations.literal: In office more than a year, treasury reserves greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year in office, treasury reserves rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 擢安徽巡撫，七年，調福建。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Anhui governor; in the seventh year he was transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Anhui, and in the seventh year was transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 有林、陳、藍、胡諸大姓糾眾械鬥，治如律。

translations.literal: The great clans Lin, Chen, Lan, and Hu gathered crowds for armed fights; he punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The great clans Lin, Chen, Lan, and Hu rallied armed factions; he punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 治海盜三腳虎及蔡牽羽黨，請祀海洋陣亡官兵，緝匪死事者一體入祀，從之。

translations.literal: He suppressed the pirate Sanjiaohu and the followers of Cai Qian, requested enshrinement of naval officers who died in battle on the seas, and that those who died catching bandits be enshrined together; the request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the pirate Sanjiaohu and Cai Qian's followers, and asked that naval officers killed at sea be enshrined together with constables who died in bandit suppression; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 十一年，蔡牽久未平，仁宗以台灣剿捕事殷，殿圖操守尚好，軍務未嫺，調江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Cai Qian had long gone unquelled; the Renzong Emperor, because Taiwan suppression was pressing, judged Diantu's integrity still good but his military affairs unskilled, and transferred him to Jiangxi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Cai Qian had still not been subdued. Because the Taiwan campaign was urgent, Emperor Renzong judged Diantu upright but unversed in military affairs and transferred him to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 尋詔斥殿圖於軍事無所陳奏，又不能禁止海口偷漏水米火藥，降四五品京堂；

translations.literal: Soon an edict rebuked Diantu for memorializing nothing on military affairs and for failing to stop smuggling of rice, gunpowder, and the like at the harbor mouth, and demoted him to a fourth- or fifth-rank Beijing appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict rebuked him for offering no counsel on military affairs and for failing to stop smuggling of grain, gunpowder, and supplies at the ports, and demoted him to a fourth- or fifth-rank post in the capital;

sentences.zh: 又以所屬久羈案犯，以中允、贊善降補。

translations.literal: again because his subordinates long detained prisoners in cases, he was demoted to fill a post as zhongyun or zanshan.
translations.idiomatic: and because his subordinates had long held prisoners without trial, he was further demoted to fill a post as Hanlin zhongyun or zanshan.

sentences.zh: 尋遷翰林院侍講，引病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hanlin lecturer and, citing illness, returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hanlin lecturer, then cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，閩浙總督文煜疏陳殿圖前任福建政績昭著，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In early Guangxu the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Wen Yu memorialized that Diantu's achievements as former Fujian administration commissioner were illustrious, and he was given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign, Fujian-Zhejiang governor-general Wen Yu memorialized that Diantu's former record in Fujian had been outstanding, and he received the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 張師誠，字蘭渚，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng, style name Lanzhu, was a native of Gui'an, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng, whose style was Lanzhu, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，南巡，召試賜舉人，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: Mid-Qianlong, during the southern tour, he was summoned for examination and granted provincial graduate status, appointed Grand Secretariat drafter, and served as Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianlong's southern tour he was summoned for examination, granted provincial graduate status, appointed a Grand Secretariat drafter, and served on the Grand Council staff.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部主事，忤和珅，緣事降中書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel; he offended Heshen and was demoted to drafter on a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, offended Heshen, and was demoted to drafter on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 得應會試，五十五年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He became eligible for the metropolitan examination; in the fifty-fifth year he became a metropolitan graduate, changed to Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took the metropolitan examination and in the fifty-fifth year passed it, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，出為山西蒲州知府，歷雁平道，河南、江蘇按察使，遷山西布政使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he went out as Shanxi Puzhou prefect, served as Yanping intendant, Henan and Jiangsu provincial judge, and was transferred to Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing he was posted as prefect of Puzhou in Shanxi, then served as Yanping intendant, provincial judge of Henan and Jiangsu, and was appointed Shanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 州縣倉庫多虧，師誠知清查有名無實，特嚴於交代之際，有虧必完，在任三年，庫儲充裕。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county treasuries were often in deficit; Shicheng knew that investigations were nominal; he was especially strict at handover—where there was deficit it must be made good; in three years in office treasury reserves were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county treasuries were often in deficit. Shicheng knew audits were mostly for show, so he was especially strict at handover: any shortfall had to be made up. After three years the stores were flush.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢江西巡撫，以兼提督賜花翎，遂著為令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Jiangxi governor; because he also held military governorship he was granted the peacock feather, and thereafter this became the established rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to governor of Jiangxi. Because he also held the military governorship, he was granted the peacock feather, and thereafter the practice was fixed as precedent.

sentences.zh: 尋調福建，清治淹牘，疏陳整頓積弊事宜，詔嘉勉。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Fujian, cleared the backlog of cases, memorialized measures to rectify accumulated abuses, and the edict praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Fujian, cleared the backlog of cases, and memorialized plans to root out long-standing abuses; the throne praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 時海盜蔡牽、硃濆方猖獗，總督玉德廢弛黜去，阿林保繼任，復與​​提督李長庚不協；

translations.literal: At the time the pirates Cai Qian and Zhu Fen were rampant; Governor Yu De was negligent and dismissed; Alinbao succeeded him but again was at odds with Regional Commander Li Changgeng;
translations.idiomatic: Pirates Cai Qian and Zhu Fen were then at their height. Governor-general Yu De was removed for negligence. Alinbao succeeded him but again clashed with Provincial Military Commander Li Changgeng;

sentences.zh: 師誠至，始嚴防海口，杜岸姦接濟，籌備船械，長庚得盡力剿捕。

translations.literal: When Shicheng arrived he first strictly guarded the harbor mouths, cut off shore traitors who supplied the pirates, and prepared ships and weapons, so Changgeng could exert his full strength in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Shicheng arrived he tightened harbor defenses, cut off shore collaborators who supplied the pirates, and stockpiled ships and arms, enabling Changgeng to press the campaign with full force.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，長庚追蔡牽於粵洋，以傷殞。

translations.literal: That winter Changgeng pursued Cai Qian in Guangdong waters and died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Changgeng pursued Cai Qian in Guangdong waters and died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 牽犯台灣後山噶仔蘭，為生番擊退，請收其地入版籍，免為賊踞。

translations.literal: Qian raided the rear of Taiwan at Kavalan and was repelled by raw savages; Shicheng requested that the land be brought into the registers lest pirates seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Qian raided Kavalan on Taiwan's eastern coast and was driven off by aboriginal tribes; Shicheng asked that the territory be registered lest pirates occupy it.

sentences.zh: 十三年，硃濆與牽有隙，獨竄閩洋，總兵許松年擊斃之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhu Fen fell out with Qian, fled alone to Fujian waters, and Regional Commander Xu Songnian attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhu Fen broke with Cai Qian, fled alone into Fujian waters, and was killed in action by regional commander Xu Songnian.

sentences.zh: 其弟渥，勢蹙思投首，會道員德華由台灣內渡，遇牽黨圍劫，渥救之，藉以通款，尋复拒敵粵師不果降。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wo, hard pressed and thinking to surrender, happened upon Circuit Intendant Dehua crossing inland from Taiwan; he encountered Qian's followers surrounding and robbing him, Wo rescued him, and used this to open negotiations; before long he again resisted Guangdong troops and the surrender did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fen's younger brother Wo, cornered and ready to surrender, happened to rescue Circuit Intendant Dehua when Dehua was crossing from Taiwan and was ambushed by Cai Qian's men. Wo used the encounter to open peace talks, but soon afterward he fought Guangdong forces again and never submitted.

sentences.zh: 十四年，阿林保調兩江，師誠暫署總督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Alinbao was transferred to the Two Jiangs, and Shicheng temporarily served as acting governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Alinbao was transferred to the Two Jiangs, and Zhang Shicheng temporarily served as acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 聞蔡牽竄浙洋，親駐廈門，提督王得祿、邱良功合剿，毀盜舟，牽墮海死。

translations.literal: Learning that Cai Qian had fled into Zhejiang waters, he personally stationed at Xiamen; admirals Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong joined in suppression, destroyed pirate vessels, and Qian fell into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Cai Qian had fled into Zhejiang waters, he took personal command at Xiamen. Admirals Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong joined the campaign, destroyed the pirate fleet, and Cai Qian fell into the sea and drowned.

sentences.zh: 硃渥尋率三千餘人歸誠，赦其罪，海疆以安，閩人刊石烏石山以紀功。

translations.literal: Zhu Wo soon led more than three thousand men in submission; their crimes were pardoned, the maritime frontier was pacified, and the people of Fujian carved a stone on Wushi Mountain to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wo soon led more than three thousand followers in surrender. Their crimes were pardoned, the coast was pacified, and the people of Fujian carved a commemorative stone on Wushi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 海寇稽誅久，由閩、浙不能合力，自師誠治閩，而阮元復蒞浙，始告成功。

translations.literal: Sea bandits had long evaded punishment because Fujian and Zhejiang could not combine forces; only after Shicheng governed Fujian and Ruan Yuan again took office in Zhejiang was success finally reported.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates had long escaped destruction because Fujian and Zhejiang could not act in concert. Only after Zhang Shicheng governed Fujian and Ruan Yuan returned to office in Zhejiang was the campaign finally brought to success.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉其嚴斷接濟，為殄寇之本。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor praised his strict cutting off of supplies as the foundation for exterminating the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong praised his rigorous blockade of pirate supply lines as the essential foundation for destroying the raiders.

sentences.zh: 京察特予獎敘。

translations.literal: At the capital inspection he was specially granted merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial capital inspection he received a special commendation for merit.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調江蘇。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 百齡為總督，諸巡撫皆承望風旨，師誠獨舉其職。

translations.literal: Bai Ling was governor-general; all provincial governors followed his lead, but Shicheng alone performed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ling was governor-general, and the other provincial governors all deferred to his wishes; Zhang Shicheng alone discharged his office conscientiously.

sentences.zh: 初彭齡奉命同查虧帑，意與百齡、師誠不合，遂劾兩人皆受餽遺，而不得實，詔原之。

translations.literal: Initially Peng Ling was ordered to investigate treasury deficits jointly; he was at odds with Bai Ling and Shicheng, and therefore impeached them both for accepting gifts, but could not prove it; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ling had been ordered to investigate treasury shortfalls jointly with them, but he was at odds with Bai Ling and Zhang Shicheng and impeached both for taking bribes. He could not substantiate the charges, and the throne pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 會百齡窮治逆書獄，閭閻悚息，巡撫所主五府州得無擾。

translations.literal: At this time Bai Ling was energetically prosecuting the literary-inquisition cases for seditious writings; the common people were terrified into silence, and the five prefectures and departments under the governor's charge were spared disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Bai Ling was vigorously prosecuting the literary-inquisition cases for seditious writings, and the common people lived in fear. The five prefectures and departments under the governor's jurisdiction were spared the worst of the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 川沙民有燒香傳徒者，有司密捕解江寧，師誠遣標弁要於途，交按察司依律鞫治，免辜磔者數十人，時以稱之。

translations.literal: In Chuansha commoners were practicing incense-burning sect teaching; officials secretly arrested them and sent them to Jiangning. Shicheng dispatched runners to intercept them on the road, handed them to the provincial judge for trial according to law, and spared several dozen innocent people from wrongful execution; contemporaries praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuansha some commoners belonged to an incense-burning sect that proselytized disciples. Officials had them secretly arrested and sent to Jiangning for trial. Zhang Shicheng dispatched military runners to intercept the prisoners on the road and turned them over to the provincial judge for lawful hearing, sparing several dozen innocent people from execution. Contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，父病篤，不俟代回籍，被嚴議褫職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year his father fell gravely ill; without waiting for his successor he returned home, and was severely censured and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year his father fell gravely ill. Without waiting for his successor he returned home, was severely censured, and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 尋予編修，服闋，遷中允。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed compiler; after mourning he was promoted to vice director of the Supervisorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Hanlin compiler; after his mourning period ended he was promoted to companion of the heir apparent (zhongyun).

sentences.zh: 歷江西、安徽布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Jiangxi and Anhui provincial administration commissioners in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢廣東巡撫，調安徽，繼母憂去官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to Guangdong governor, transferred to Anhui, and left office on account of his stepmother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to governor of Guangdong, then transferred to Anhui, and left office to observe mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 复歷山西、江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: He again served as Shanxi and Jiangsu governors in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he served in succession as governor of Shanxi and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 六年，召授倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of the grain transport offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was summoned to court and appointed vice minister of the grain transport offices.

sentences.zh: 以病乞歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: He begged leave on account of illness and returned home, dying at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire on grounds of illness, returned home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 師誠警敏綜覈，在當時疆吏中有能名，治福建最著，繼之者為王紹蘭。

translations.literal: Shicheng was alert and comprehensive in judgment; among frontier officials of the day he had a reputation for ability, and his governance of Fujian was most renowned; his successor was Wang Shaolan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng was quick-witted and thorough in administration. Among frontier officials of his day he enjoyed a reputation for ability, and his service in Fujian was especially celebrated. His successor was Wang Shaolan.

sentences.zh: 紹蘭，字南陔，浙江蕭山人。

translations.literal: Shaolan, styled Nan'ai, was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaolan, styled Nan'ai, was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十八年進士，授福建南屏知縣，調閩縣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Fujian, and was transferred to Min county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year of Qianlong he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Fujian, and was later transferred to Min county.

sentences.zh: 巡撫汪志伊薦其治行，仁宗曰：「王紹蘭好官，朕早聞其名。」

translations.literal: Governor Wang Zhiyi recommended his administrative conduct; the Renzong Emperor said: "Wang Shaolan is a good official—I have long heard his name."
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Zhiyi recommended his record in office. Emperor Renzong said, "Wang Shaolan is an excellent official. I have long heard his name."

sentences.zh: 召入見，以知州用，擢泉州知府。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience, appointed at the rank of prefect, and promoted to Quanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for an audience, appointed at prefectural rank, and promoted to prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉兩郡多械鬥，自紹蘭治泉州，民俗漸馴，而漳州守令以械鬥獄獲罪，詔舉紹蘭以為法。

translations.literal: Zhang and Quan prefectures had many armed brawls; from the time Shaolan governed Quanzhou popular customs gradually grew tame, while Zhangzhou prefects and magistrates were punished in armed-brawl cases; an edict held Shaolan up as the model.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were notorious for armed clan feuds. Under Shaolan's governance of Quanzhou popular customs gradually grew more orderly, while Zhangzhou prefects and magistrates were punished for mishandling feud cases. An edict held Shaolan up as the model to follow.

sentences.zh: 擢興泉永道，捕獲蔡牽養子蔡三及其黨蔡昌等，予議敘。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Xingquan Yong circuit intendant, captured Cai Qian's adopted son Cai San and his follower Cai Chang and others, and was granted merit citation.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to intendant of the Xingquan Yong circuit, captured Cai Qian's adopted son Cai San and his follower Cai Chang among others, and received a merit citation.

sentences.zh: 遷按察使，母憂去，服闋，起故官，就遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial judge; on his mother's death he left office; after mourning he resumed his former post and was promoted in place to provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial judge, left office on his mother's death, and after mourning resumed his former post and was promoted in place to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十九年，擢巡撫，始終未出福建。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to governor and never left Fujian thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Jiaqing he was promoted to governor and never left Fujian for the rest of his career.

sentences.zh: 尋汪志伊來為​​總督，與布政使李賡芸不合，因訐告受賂，劾治，屬吏希指羅織，賡芸憤而自縊。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Zhiyi came as governor-general; he did not get along with Administration Commissioner Li Gengyun, and on a charge of taking bribes had him impeached and prosecuted; subordinate officials seized the cue to fabricate cases, and Gengyun hanged himself in indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Zhiyi arrived as governor-general. He clashed with Administration Commissioner Li Gengyun, denounced him for taking bribes, and had him impeached and prosecuted. Subordinate officials took the hint and fabricated charges against him, and Gengyun hanged himself in despair.
